name: Kelenga
catalog_citation: Heath, Jeffrey. 2023. A Grammar of Kelenga (Hainyaxo), Bozo language of Mali. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.7699838 (file 'Kelenga Bozo grammar ').

catalog_quote: 3.1.2 Word-internal metrical structure. Since syncope and accentual processes are rare in Kelenga, there is not much to say about foot structure. CvCvCv words do not syncopate systematically to CvCCv, although when C2 is r it allows optional syncope of the second vowel: màrìfá-à ~ màrfá-à 'rifle'. There is no well-defined stress system as such. Whereas some languages of the zone allow only one H-toned peak (whether on a single mora or syllable or spread over multiple syllables), Kelenga allows two peaks in noun stems, as in téèndáŋ-ɔ̀ 'hamerkop (bird)' and tómóndìgí-ì 'ricin (shrub)'. There is no sensitivity to overall prosodic weight of stems in affixal morphology. ... [p. 45] Since prefixes do not occur in Kelenga morphology and since there is no well-defined stress system, it is not possible to distinguish proclitics from prefixes by phonological criteria. ... audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The no-word-stress coding rests on the only reference grammar of the language (Heath 2023, 619 pp, open access), which we hold; the deciding sentences ('There is no well-defined stress system as such', 'the absence of stress') are verbatim at sec. 3.1.2 p. 21 and sec. 3.5 p. 45-46, and sec. 3.6 confirms prosody is lexical H/L tone with stem melodies. Heath's scattered remarks attributing low pitch of particles bí/gà to 'lack of stress' (pp. ~296, 459) are phrase-level allegro effects on grammatical particles, not a word-stress system, and do not disturb the classification. Glottolog and Zenodo show no newer or more specialised prosodic study. Minor locator nit only: the clitics sentence sits at the p. 45/46 boundary. no reclassification, no upgrade needed.
